mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Incorporation of Taiwan parent company (Company Registration Information)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Taiwan Ministry of Economic Affairs (MOEA) Company Registration Authority
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Taiwan notary public -> district court notarization certification -> Straits Exchange Foundation (SEF) transmission of notarized copy -> Association for Relations Across the Taiwan Straits (ARATS) verification -> PRC counterparty accepts. Taiwan is not a Hague Apostille Convention Contracting Party, so no Hague Apostille is available; use this functional consular legalization path only and never chain it with an apostille path.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Good Standing or Taiwan tax/corporate filing status certificate
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Taiwan Ministry of Economic Affairs and/or National Taxation Bureau
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Taiwan notary public -> SEF -> ARATS verification for use in Mainland China; for a non-Apostille third country, Taiwan Ministry of Foreign Affairs countersignature followed by destination-state consular legalization; for an Apostille Contracting State, the competent authority must issue the apostille on PRC-origin documents, not on Taiwan documents; the paths are mutually exclusive and must not be combined.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Board Resolution or Power of Attorney authorizing WFOE formation
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Taiwan parent company board of directors or shareholders' meeting
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Notarize signature and corporate seal in Taiwan -> SEF transmission to ARATS for verification -> SAMR filing; alternatively, if the entity is a PRC-origin signer, notarize in Mainland China -> PRC Ministry of Foreign Affairs apostille for Apostille Convention states, or -> SEF/ARATS verification for Taiwan use; never sequence apostille and SEF/ARATS.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Draft Articles of Association of the WFOE (charter)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: WFOE sole shareholder or initial incorporator
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: PRC notary public -> provincial notary association sends notarized copies to SEF for Taiwan recognition, or -> PRC Ministry of Foreign Affairs apostille when the charter will be used in an Apostille Convention state; these are parallel alternatives, with no chaining permitted.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Bank Reference Letter for Taiwan parent or WFOE opening bank
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Commercial bank in Taiwan or Mainland China
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Bank officer authorized-signature verification and notarization; Taiwan bank letters must be notarized in Taiwan -> SEF -> ARATS verification for PRC use; Mainland China bank letters must be notarized -> PRC MFA apostille for foreign use; for non-Apostille states, consular legalization by the destination country's consulate is required after diplomatic authentication; do not chain with SEF/ARATS unless the destination is Taiwan.

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Enhanced due diligence is mandatory for all beneficial owners, directors, senior managers, authorized signatories and material IP licensees. Screen continuously against OFAC SDN List, UN Security Council Consolidated List, EU consolidated sanctions, PRC MOFCOM/MFA sanctions and anti-terrorism lists, Ministry of Public Security wanted and terrorist lists, Taiwan Financial Supervisory Commission sanctions/PEP registries, and adverse media on money laundering, corruption and tax evasion. Verify identity from passports and corporate registers, require source-of-funds and source-of-wealth evidence, and apply the 25% ownership threshold for UBO identification. Re-screen every 90 days and upon any trigger event; escalate positive PEP/sanctions hits within 24 hours to the designated AML compliance officer and file a Suspicious Transaction Report with PBOC where required.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: State Administration for Market Regulation (SAMR) Enterprise Name Self-Service Declaration and Registration System, integrated with the National Enterprise Credit Information Publicity System (NECIPS)
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: The WFOE must have a registered name in simplified Chinese characters, following the four-tier naming convention: administrative division + distinctive trade name/font + industry description + organizational form. Pinyin or English words cannot substitute for the Chinese registered name. Phonetic transliteration of the Taiwan parent's English or traditional-Chinese name must be provided, but the registered WFOE name must use simplified Chinese. A separate English translation may be recorded for banking and licensing, but only the Chinese name carries legal personality.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: Obtain the written SAMR rejection notice stating the statutory basis. File an administrative reconsideration application with the SAMR authority at the next higher level within 60 days of receipt, or file an administrative lawsuit in the competent people's court within 6 months under the PRC Administrative Litigation Law. The applicant may simultaneously submit up to three alternative qualified name strings. If rejection is based on prior third-party rights, request administrative adjudication of the name dispute or obtain the prior registrant's written consent. A rejected name string is generally released within 30 days and may be re-filed after that date.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Virtual office or commercial-mailbox-only addresses are not acceptable as the WFOE registered office in this IP HoldCo structure. PRC tax authorities, SAMR and banks require a physical leased office evidenced by a lease agreement with a term exceeding one year, a copy of the landlord's property ownership certificate, rental invoices, on-site signage, and local personnel records. PBOC Order No. 1 and BEPS Action 5/8-10 commercial substance expectations further require local management decisions, books and records, transfer pricing documentation, and physical servers or equipment commensurate with the royalty licensing activity. A virtual office may be used only as an ancillary administrative address and never as the registered office.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: High: estimated 70% probability of an unannounced on-site inspection within the first 18 months after registration, because the entity is classified Medium_Risk_Enhanced with intercompany royalty flows. Checklist: (1) original lease contract and rental receipts; (2) utility bills; (3) payroll and social insurance contribution records for local employees; (4) bank statements and tax filing proof; (5) presence of computers, servers, IP-related records and board meeting minutes; (6) physical signage on the registered address; (7) absence of mailbox-only indicators. Municipal tax bureaus and SAMR may inspect upon issuance of the first royalty invoice or on any cross-border payment trigger.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Company Law of the People's Republic of China (revised 2023, effective 1 July 2024), Articles 1-12, 23-25, 43-48, 57-65, 211-216; Foreign Investment Law of the People's Republic of China (2019), Articles 2, 4, 6, 28-31 and 33; Regulations on the Administration of Market Entity Registration (2021), Articles 8-20; Provisions on Foreign Investment Information Reporting and Investment Protection (2020), Articles 3-15.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: State Administration for Market Regulation (SAMR) and the local Market Regulation Administration having territorial jurisdiction over the registered office of the WFOE.
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Application for Establishment Registration of a Foreign-Invested Limited Liability Company, together with the Articles of Association and the Foreign Investment Information Report, submitted through SAMR National Enterprise Registration Online System.
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: None. Chinese company law and the Foreign Investment Law impose no statutory minimum paid-up capital for a WFOE engaged in IP licensing and do not require a blocked escrow account. The sole foreign shareholder must state a subscribed registered capital in the Articles of Association, contribute such capital within the contribution period specified therein, bear joint and several liability if other shareholders fail to make their own capital contributions, and may not reduce capital below zero unless a lawful capital reduction is registered. Unpaid capital remains a debt of the shareholder to the company.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: PRO-FORMA FIRST BOARD RESOLUTION OF CN_WFOE_LTD, A WHOLLY FOREIGN-OWNED LIMITED LIABILITY COMPANY UNDER THE LAWS OF THE PEOPLE'S REPUBLIC OF CHINA. WHEREAS the sole shareholder has resolved to form the company for the purpose of owning, monetizing, cross-licensing and sub-licensing patents, trademarks, copyrights, know-how and related intellectual property rights on a global basis under ISIC 6420; WHEREAS the Articles of Association have been prepared and adopted as the constitutional instrument of the company; WHEREAS the company intends to open bank accounts, receive intercompany royalties, and remit lawful dividends or service fees; and WHEREAS the laws of the People's Republic of China require the company to maintain a registered office, appoint statutory officers, and adopt proper corporate governance before transacting business. NOW, THEREFORE, the sole shareholder and the first board of directors, acting unanimously, hereby resolve as follows: 1. Share Capital Subscription. The registered capital of the company is fixed at the amount set out in the Articles of Association. The sole shareholder subscribes to one hundred percent of the registered capital and agrees to pay the subscribed capital in cash or in kind within the contribution period specified in the Articles of Association. The board shall not accept a subscription above the registered capital and shall not return contributed capital except through a lawful reduction approved by the shareholder and registered with the State Administration for Market Regulation. 2. Banking Authorization. The company shall open a basic deposit account and an onshore foreign currency capital account at a bank licensed in the People's Republic of China. The legal representative and the finance officer, acting jointly or singly as indicated in the bank mandate, are hereby authorized to execute account opening applications, sign specimen signature cards, issue payment and wire transfer instructions, submit foreign exchange registration forms, negotiate loan and banking agreements, and otherwise manage the company bank accounts. All initial capital contributions, royalty receipts and intercompany payments shall be deposited only into the company accounts and disbursed in accordance with Chinese foreign exchange and anti-money laundering rules. 3. Registered Office Adoption. The registered office described in the Articles of Association is adopted as the official domicile of the company for service of process, statutory notices, tax correspondence and all regulatory filings. The board shall maintain the lease agreement, property ownership certificate and usage license at such office, shall keep the corporate seal and statutory books there, and shall file an amendment registration with the Market Regulation Administration within 30 days of any relocation. 4. Statutory Officer Appointments. The following persons are appointed to the offices set beside their names: [Legal Representative and General Manager], [Finance Officer], and [Compliance Officer or Company Secretary]. Each such officer shall have the powers and fiduciary duties prescribed by law and the Articles of Association. The legal representative is authorized to sign contracts and filings, appear before authorities, and bind the company in ordinary course transactions; provided that all IP licensing agreements, royalty rates, transfer pricing arrangements, and contracts involving a value above the threshold established by the board must first be approved by the shareholder. 5. Corporate Governance and Statutory Compliance. The board shall implement tax registration, invoicing, accounting, payroll, social insurance, annual reporting, foreign investment information reporting, and intellectual property licensing recordation procedures before the first licensing transaction closes. The fiscal year runs from the date of establishment to 31 December and ends annually thereafter. 6. Ratification and Effective Date. All acts lawfully performed by the promoter before the date of this resolution to prepare for incorporation are ratified, confirmed and adopted. This resolution is effective immediately upon execution and may be amended only by a subsequent resolution of the sole shareholder or board of directors. Dated at [Place], on [Date], signed by the sole shareholder and the chairman of the board.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Name Availability Review, Business Scope Alignment, and Shareholder Identity Verification
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: SAMR National Enterprise Registration Online System (neris.samr.gov.cn) and the local Market Regulation Administration
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Log in to the SAMR enterprise registration portal using the legal representative or agent real-name authenticated account; submit two or three proposed company names, the exact business scope corresponding to ISIC 6420 and NAICS 533110, and the planned registered capital. The system will compare the proposed names against nationwide databases and flag names identical or confusingly similar to existing enterprises. The applicant must also upload the Taiwanese shareholder certificate of incorporation or equivalent identity document, certify the beneficial ownership and intended capital contribution amount, ensure the scope does not fall within the Foreign Investment Negative List, and reserve the approved name. The local Market Regulation Administration will query the name in its internal registry and issue or withhold the Name Pre-Approval Notice. After approval, the name reservation is generally valid for six months and the applicant may proceed to full incorporation filing.
required_dossiers: Two or three proposed company names in Chinese and English
Planned business scope aligned with ISIC 6420 and NAICS 533110
Shareholder's notarized certificate of incorporation and valid passport or equivalent identity document
Shareholder resolution authorizing the filing and appointment of local agent
Power of attorney if an agent is engaged
Details of proposed registered capital and contribution period
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the name is rejected or placed under suspension, the applicant must review the conflict notice, modify the proposed name by adding a distinctive industry or geographic qualifier, or appeal to the local Market Regulation Administration within 15 days of the rejection notice; a re-filed application receives a new reference number and resumed review.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Execution and Notarization of the Articles of Association and Submission of Establishment Registration Application
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Local Market Regulation Administration enterprise registration service window, with notarization by a competent notary public when required
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Finalize the Chinese and English Articles of Association signed by the sole shareholder, including company name, address, registered capital, contribution period, shareholder rights, governance organs, legal representative, business scope and liquidation provisions. Notarize the shareholder resolution and the authorization for the legal representative where local practice demands. Complete the Application for Establishment Registration of a Foreign-Invested Limited Liability Company, affix the foreign investor company seal and proposed company seal, and submit the package online or at the local Market Regulation Administration service window. The authority will review legality, capital adequacy, directors and supervisors information, and the exact business scope. If the scope is outside the negative list and no sectoral approval is required, registration may proceed without prior approval; if the scope triggers licensing, the approval certificate must be included. Ensure the foreign investment information report section is filled in and acknowledge that the registration becomes effective only when the certificate is issued.
required_dossiers: Completed Application for Establishment Registration of a Foreign-Invested Limited Liability Company
Signed Articles of Association in duplicate
Original or certified copy of the lease contract and property ownership certificate for the registered office
Notarized and authenticated certificate of incorporation of the Taiwanese shareholder and its board resolution
Power of attorney appointing the local agent and legal representative
Name Pre-Approval Notice
Foreign Investment Information Report form
Identification documents of directors, supervisor and legal representative
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If an application is queried or suspended, the applicant must reply in writing to the SAMR notice within 10 working days, correct the documentary defects, resubmit the revised electronic version through the portal, and pay any required notarization fee; failure to cure will result in refusal and the applicant may file an administrative reconsideration with the higher-level Market Regulation Administration within 60 days.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Business License Issuance, Corporate Seal Carving, Tax and Social Security Registration Activation, and Bank Account Opening
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Local Market Regulation Administration; Public Security Bureau-authorized seal engraving enterprise; State Taxation Administration local tax office; Ministry of Human Resources and Social Security; and a People's Bank of China-licensed bank for basic deposit account and SAFE FDI registration
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: After SAMR grants registration, the company receives the business license containing the unified social credit code. Immediately thereafter, arrange the legal representative identification, engage the Public Security Bureau-licensed engraver to produce the company seal, financial seal, legal representative seal and invoice seal, and register each seal with the required police filing. Complete tax registration by activating the tax registration in the electronic tax service system, setting up the electronic invoice scheme and payroll registration; complete social insurance and housing fund registration for employees, and open the basic deposit account and general settlement account at a licensed bank. The bank shall automatically report the basic deposit account information to the People's Bank of China. The foreign investor must complete foreign direct investment (FDI) registration through the bank with the State Administration of Foreign Exchange for any paid-in capital remittances and for onward intercompany royalty flows.
required_dossiers: Original business license and unified social credit code certificate
Legal representative and shareholder identification documents
Certificate of residence or lease for the registered office
Seal engraving registration form
Tax registration forms and bank account opening documents
Articles of Association and board resolution appointing officers
FDI registration application and foreign exchange forms
Employment contract forms and social insurance registration forms
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the bank or tax office rejects the account or registration application due to incomplete documentation, the company must obtain a written deficiency notice, rectify the missing item within five working days, and resubmit through the bank manager or tax service window; if SAFE rejects the FDI registration, re-submit a revised application with the bank after amending the beneficial ownership and foreign investor identity details.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Post-Registration Statutory Filings, Intellectual Property License Recordation and Transfer Pricing Compliance
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Ministry of Commerce via the integrated Foreign Investment Information Reporting System; State Administration for Market Regulation annual enterprise credit reporting system; State Taxation Administration and local tax authority; China National Intellectual Property Administration for license recordation; State Administration of Foreign Exchange for balance-of-payments reporting
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Within 20 days after registration, file the final Foreign Investment Information Report with the Ministry of Commerce or through the integrated SAMR and SAFE platform, reporting ultimate beneficial owners, actual control, capital contribution and any changes within 30 days. Register for VAT general taxpayer status if projected royalty income exceeds the threshold; issue VAT invoices on Chinese-source royalties and perform withholding and filing on payments to non-residents if required. Maintain statutory corporate records including the register of shareholders, minutes of board resolutions, accounting ledgers, bank statements, and contracts. For trademark or patent licenses, record the license contracts with CNIPA within 60 days after execution to perfect them against third parties. Implement transfer pricing documentation policies for cross-border royalty payments to the Taiwan parent and prepare contemporaneous documentation before the annual corporate income tax filing. The annual report must be filed with SAMR through the enterprise credit information system before 30 June each year, and foreign exchange reporting must be updated if cross-border service transactions are subject to balance-of-payments statistics.
required_dossiers: Foreign Investment Information Report
Audited financial statements or interim accounts
VAT and corporate income tax registration certificates
IP license agreements and CNIPA recordation forms
Board minutes and shareholder resolutions
Register of shareholders and share transfer records
Transfer pricing contemporaneous documentation
Annual report data and enterprise credit information filing
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Ministry of Commerce or tax authority issues a correction notice for incomplete or inconsistent information, the company shall submit a supplementary statement and revised filing within 15 working days; if CNIPA records the license late, the recordal is still possible but may not have retroactive effect against bona fide third parties, so immediate re-filing and payment of any late fee is required; for transfer pricing disputes, the taxpayer may file a mutual agreement procedure or apply for an advance pricing arrangement.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Not Applicable. ISIC 6420 activities are ownership and cross-border sub-licensing of trademarks and patents; the WFOE has no manufacturing, chemical, assembly, warehousing, or

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: State Taxation Administration of the People's Republic of China (STA), acting through local tax service bureaus; online portal is the National Electronic Tax Administration (e-Tax) system and the provincial-level Electronic Tax Bureau platforms.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: Step 1: Complete name pre-approval and incorporation with the local State Administration for Market Regulation (SAMR); the issued Business License contains the Unified Social Credit Code (USCC), which is the statutory Tax Identification Number (TIN) for all tax purposes. Step 2: Within 30 days of the license date, apply for tax registration through the STA Electronic Tax Administration; this creates the VAT, Enterprise Income Tax, withholding, and invoice registration records. Step 3: Apply for general VAT taxpayer status through the same portal when annual taxable sales will exceed CNY 5,000,000 or when input VAT refunds are required; attach the accounting and bookkeeping system evidence requested by the competent tax office. Step 4: For a foreign non-resident enterprise without a permanent establishment in mainland China, obtain non-resident tax registration or establish a withholding record with the competent tax office of the payer, submit the applicable tax residence certificate for treaty or cross-border arrangement relief, and ensure the local payer handles withholding on royalties at the statutory rate. Step 5: Open a RMB and foreign-currency bank account, complete SAFE foreign exchange registration for trade in goods and services, and link the bank account to the export proceeds monitoring environment used by the STA for export rebate verification.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: None. PRC tax law does not provide check-the-box or hybrid mismatch elections; all limited liability enterprises are taxed as standalone resident entities. The only optional status is small-scale vs general VAT taxpayer status, which is an indirect tax registration election and does not change the entity-level enterprise income tax classification.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: CNY 5,000,000 annual taxable sales (mandatory general VAT taxpayer registration); below that threshold the entity remains a small-scale VAT taxpayer unless voluntary general registration is approved. Basic tax registration is mandatory within 30 days of business license issuance irrespective of turnover.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: The STA requires fully digitalised electronic invoices through the National Electronic Invoice Service Platform and the Electronic Tax Administration. Invoices are issued in near real-time and transmitted via API/e-invoice interfaces to the STA, with a unique digital tax-control code and anti-counterfeiting digital seal. General VAT taxpayers must verify incoming invoices on the VAT Invoice Comprehensive Service Platform before claiming input tax credits; high-volume issuers must integrate ERP systems through the tax authority APIs for automatic invoice clearance. No physical fiscal stamping device is used for fully digitalised invoices, but all invoice data are reconciled in the STA Golden Tax system.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Goods exports qualify for zero-rating only if the goods are physically exported from mainland China and released by China Customs, the exporter is a registered VAT general taxpayer, and the export proceeds are collected from abroad within the statutory period. Services qualify for zero-rating only when listed in the cross-border zero-rated services catalogue (for example, international transportation, research and development, design and offshore software services) and are provided to an overseas recipient for use wholly outside mainland China. For patent and trademark sub-licensing, the WFOE must prove the licensed IP is economically used outside mainland China, the royalty is paid from outside mainland China (including Taiwan), and the transaction is not a domestic licence; otherwise the standard 6% VAT applies.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration (China Customs Export Goods Declaration, equivalent to an export bill of entry) showing the exported goods and HS classification
Bill of Lading (or Air Waybill for air cargo) naming an offshore consignee
Inward Remittance Certificate (FIRC) or, for mainland China, the SAFE-monitored bank export collection and foreign exchange receipt certificate evidencing repatriation of export/royalty proceeds
Export VAT refund/zero-rate application set and electronic export rebate data filed through the STA e-Tax system
Cross-border licence or royalty agreement and overseas-usage documentation substantiating that the IP is consumed outside mainland China
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: The STA and the General Administration of Customs cross-check customs declarations, transport documents, invoice data, bank FX receipts and rebate claims using the Golden Tax and Golden Customs systems. If zero-rating/refund is unsupported, falsified, or the proceeds are not repatriated within 180 days, the STA will deny the zero rate, claw back the VAT refund and input credits, apply a late-payment surcharge of 0.05% per day, and impose an administrative penalty of 50% to five times the tax shortfall under the Law on the Administration of Tax Levying and Collection. Cases involving forged export declarations, false bills of lading, or fabricated receipts are prosecuted as export tax fraud or false invoice crimes under the Criminal Law, with monetary fines, confiscation, imprisonment of responsible officers, customs fines, and revocation of expedited customs privileges.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: State Administration of Foreign Exchange (SAFE) of the People's Bank of China (PBOC)
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: SAFE administers a conditional convertibility regime for the onshore CNY currency. The WFOE will enjoy automatic convertibility for all current-account transactions, including royalty payments and intercompany service fees, provided the bank verifies the underlying license agreement, commercial invoice, tax-withholding certificate, and the WFOE's SAFE registration. Capital-account transactions—equity injections, shareholder loans, and cross-border contributions for IP assets—remain regulated and require project-wise filing or registration with SAFE before conversion. Profit repatriation and IP royalty remittances to a Taiwan parent are classified as income remittances under current account and require the WFOE to prove actual economic substance, file enterprise income tax, and withhold tax; the bank will then release the foreign exchange after a one-time documentary review. There is no surrender requirement for export proceeds; enterprises may retain export receipts in foreign currency indefinitely or settle into CNY at will. However, capital-account settlement is subject to the negative list prohibiting investments in excise levies, securities markets, real estate beyond operational needs, and interbank lending. The overall policy objective is to channel cross-border IP royalty flows through verified banks while preserving capital account administrative controls.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: Export foreign-currency receipts must be repatriated into a designated foreign-exchange settlement account at a SAFE licensed bank within 90 days of the customs export date unless an extension is approved; the mandatory conversion requirement has been eliminated, so the enterprise may retain 100% of the receipt in foreign currency or settle it into RMB at its discretion. The bank and SAFE will reconcile the receipts against the Export Verification System and customs data before the funds are made available for domestic use or onward external disbursement.

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Offshore fintech EMI platforms (Wise, Revolut, Airwallex, etc.) are not permissible as primary banking rails for the CN WFOE. The PBOC/SAFE framework requires cross-border payments and current-account settlements to be processed through domestic banks that have obtained the foreign-exchange settlement and sale license; none of the pure offshore EMIs meet this requirement, and PRC law prohibits them from opening local CNY accounts or providing capital-account services to a resident entity. They may assist only in non-onshore collection/dollar corridors, but all statutory compliance—capital verification, tax filing, and SAFE reporting—must sit with a domestic Tier-1 bank.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: For a PRC WFOE, the statutory legal representative and/or the authorized senior local manager must appear in person at the branch for the initial KYC interview; remote video-only onboarding is not accepted by all banks. Foreign directors located in Taiwan may execute a notarized power of attorney (certified through the cross-strait authentication process or consular legalization) appointing a China-based financial officer, who must attend the bank in person. The bank will require original company chops, board resolutions, and the SAIC license before any account is opened.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: UBO chain without clear natural-person attribution: the applicant's registered shareholding is held by a Taiwan holding company with nominee or conduit indications.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Provide (i) a notarized and legally authenticated Certificate of Incumbency and Register of Members of the immediate Taiwan shareholder; (ii) a UBO declaration with passport copies for every natural person holding more than 25% in two continuous tiers; (iii) a full corporate chart with tax identification numbers signed by the company secretary; and (iv) a non-nominee undertaking from the ultimate parent confirming no bearer shares.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: IP asset valuation misrepresentation: bank compliance questions whether the patent family is active and economically real rather than a synthetic royalty flow.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Provide (i) official registration certificates from CNIPA, TIPO, USPTO and equivalent offices for the core patents and trademarks; (ii) an independent valuation report prepared by a licensed CPA or registered valuer using income or market approach; (iii) the executed patent and trademark license and sub-license agreements; (iv) historical royalty invoices and bank statements showing at least 12 months of actual collections and payments; and (v) a notarized statutory declaration on the business exclusivity and licensed territories.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Source of wealth and capital injection concerns: the inbound equity contribution originates from an account not owned by the principal shareholder or from a low-tax jurisdiction with no economic substance.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Provide (i) bank reference letters and six-month bank statements from the Taiwan parent's home bank; (ii) audited financial statements for the past three fiscal years; (iii) tax returns or a Certificate of Residence; (iv) a formal board resolution authorizing the equity injection and stating the exact source of funds; and (v) a funds-transfer chain from the ultimate source to the remitting account, satisfying SAFE's same-name remittance principle.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Sanctions, embargo, and Taiwan/China cross-strait restrictions: concerns about restricted-party screening and potential dual-use technology transfer underlying the licensed patents.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Provide (i) a compliance attestation from the licensor confirming no OFAC, EU, UN, or PRC restricted party involvement; (ii) an export-control classification analysis (e.g., US ECCN or EU dual-use list) and a Technology Control Plan; (iii) any government import license or regulatory permit for controlled technology; (iv) a board resolution approving the license and committing to no re-export to sanctioned end users; and (v) end-user and customs declarations for each licensed territory.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: The Taiwan parent must initiate a SWIFT MT103 remittance to the WFOE's foreign-currency capital account at a designated Tier-1 bank. The remitter's account must be in the same legal entity name as the shareholder recorded with SAFE; the purpose code must be the SAFE FDI-to-Enterprise Capital Injection code (e.g., 621904 or bank-designated), and the reference must state the WFOE's SAFE Foreign-Investment Registration Number. Upon receipt, the bank enters the credit into the Cross-Border Income/Expenditure Direct Reporting System; a licensed PRC CPA then issues a capital verification report to prove the paid-in contribution. Capital withdrawals and settlements are allowed only after the SAFE negative-list review and must be used solely for the company's operational purpose.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: For royalty and IP sub-licensing fees, the standard rail is SWIFT MT103 corporate-to-corporate wire, preceded by a tax-payment certificate for withholding WHT and a license invoice. The bank will match the payment to an underlying license agreement in the SAFE current-account records. When disbursements relate to goods with embedded IP, a Commercial Letter of Credit (SWIFT MT700) or Documentary Collection (MT400) can be used through the bank's trade desk; for pure IP royalties, the LC/DC route is less common but permissible if the transaction is structured as technology transfer. All outward payments must be reported with the appropriate purpose code and no cash-conversion circularity.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Onshore CNY/USD, CNY/TWD, and CNY/EUR plain-vanilla forward contracts executed against underlying royalty licence exposure
Cross-currency swaps for hedging capital account exposures arising from Taiwan parent shareholder loans or intercompany debts
OTC European FX options for hedging forecast royalty receipts, subject to SAFE derivatives registration
Non-deliverable forwards are prohibited onshore for CNY; the WFOE may not use offshore NDF contracts

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Profit-Seeking Enterprise Income Tax Return
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Ministry of Finance, National Taxation Bureau
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: 31 May of the following calendar year for calendar-year taxpayers; within 4 months after fiscal year-end if a different fiscal year is used
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late payment surcharge of 3% of the unpaid tax per 30-day period, up to 10%; additional understatement penalty of up to 20%; daily interest accrues until full payment; tax authorities may attach bank accounts and assets.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Beneficial Owner and Shareholding Structure Confirmation
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Ministry of Economic Affairs, Company Registration Database
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 5 months after the end of each fiscal year (normally by 31 May for calendar-year companies); intermediate changes in directors, supervisors, managers, or shareholders holding 10% or more must be reported within 15 days of the change
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Administrative fine of TWD 50,000–500,000 per violation; responsible officers may be fined separately; willful non-compliance may lead to dissolution or striking-off by order of the competent authority.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Statutory Accounts Approval and Shareholders' Meeting Record
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Ministry of Economic Affairs (if director re-election or amendment registration is triggered); otherwise retained in the statutory minute book
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Ordinary shareholders' meeting must be held by 30 June for a calendar-year company; minutes must be prepared and kept with the statutory books
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to hold an annual shareholders' meeting allows shareholders to convene it at company expense; the competent authority may order remedial action and impose fines on responsible persons; repeated non-compliance may result in involuntary dissolution.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: A Taiwan limited company is required to have financial statements audited and certified by an independent CPA when paid-in capital exceeds TWD 30 million (approximately USD 1 million), or when it is a financial institution, public company, or special regulated industry; otherwise audit is generally voluntary unless required by lenders or shareholders.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Public companies must apply Taiwan-IFRS (TIFRS); non-public companies must follow the Business Entity Accounting Act, the Business Entity Accounting Regulations, and Taiwan-IFRS or the SME IFRS framework as applicable.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: Under Company Act Article 22-1, a non-public company must annually confirm and file with the Ministry of Economic Affairs the list of directors, supervisors, managers, and direct or indirect shareholders holding more than 10% of shares or voting rights; any shareholding transfer causing a change must be filed within 15 days.
